title: Elasticsearch 9.6: Query Amazon S3 data in place, multiuser chat, and PDFs to Markdown
summary: Elasticsearch 9.6 queries S3 files without ingesting them, runs existing Grafana dashboard queries via PromQL, and pulls clean Markdown out of scanned PDFs.
body_markdown:
[Elasticsearch](https://elastic.co/elasticsearch) 9.6 now helps you query


your files directly in Amazon S3, using Elasticsearch Query Language ([ES|QL](https://www.elastic.co/docs/explore-analyze/query-filter/languages/esql) ), without ingestion. Prometheus Query Language (PromQL) coverage is up to 92% of the queries used in the top 100 Grafana dashboards, so your existing dashboards run unchanged against Elasticsearch. Plus,[Kibana](https://elastic.co/kibana) chat now supports multiple users and agents in one conversation. Point the new` document_extraction`[inference](https://www.elastic.co/docs/explore-analyze/elastic-inference) task type at a PDF, and clean Markdown comes back in one request. Chat keeps working behind proxies that block streaming, and opt-in prompt caching cuts cost on multi-turn agent workflows. Elastic Service Accounts keep scheduled automation running when its author changes teams, and budget alerts and audit logs help admin track spend and changes. Read on to learn more about these new capabilities.

## Query S3 data in place with ES|QL


Archived logs and CloudTrail records often sit in S3, as do vendor feeds, and querying them used to mean indexing


them first or running a second query engine. With ES|QL Data Federation, you register a data source, name a dataset, and then query Parquet, CSV, TSV, and NDJSON files with the same ES|QL syntax and Kibana workflows that you use for indexed data. Elasticsearch 9.6 adds a guided Kibana setup with keyless federated identity, along with support for the Kibana time picker and dashboard time range. It also adds partition and folder pruning that skips files outside the queried time range.


ES|QL Data Federation is in technical preview, for:


- Enterprise subscriptions only.
- Stateful deployments only (Elastic Cloud Hosted \[ECH\] and Elastic Self-Managed), with Elastic Serverless coming soon.
- Amazon S3 only.


Read[the ES|QL Data Federation documentation](https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/query-languages/esql/esql-data-federation) .


## More ES|QL capabilities in 9.6: Logical Views, LOOKUP JOIN, and subqueries


Further ES|QL updates make queries easier to reuse and filter. Logical Views (generally available \[GA\]) lets you save an ES|QL query once and call it with` FROM my_view` , so one update reaches every dashboard, rule, and query that uses it. Each view query runs on live data with the caller's permissions. Coordinator-mode` LOOKUP JOIN` (GA, Enterprise) lets cross-cluster and cross-project queries join against a lookup index that exists only on the coordinating cluster, so you don't have to copy it to every remote cluster.


` IN` and` NOT IN` subqueries (GA) keep filter logic in a single statement.` WHERE source.ip NOT IN (FROM allowed_ips | KEEP ip)` matches rows against a list that another ES|QL query computes, all in one statement. This pattern works in production detection rules, such as dynamic deny-lists and exception lists. Elasticsearch 9.6 also adds subqueries that return multiple columns.


## Run columnar analytics in Elasticsearch with Columnar Mode


We’re continuing to build on[Columnar Mode](https://www.elastic.co/search-labs/blog/data-platform-consolidation-elasticsearch) (currently in technical preview). In Elasticsearch 9.6, we’ve added faster aggregations on high-cardinality fields and a columnar codec (both technical preview) that applies dictionary encoding to multi-value keyword fields to speed up analytical queries and reduce storage. Columnar Mode lets you run search, vector


retrieval


, and analytics on the same data in one Elasticsearch cluster. You don't need a second columnar database with its own ingest pipeline and query language, or another security model to manage. It does this by keeping a single columnar copy of each field instead of an inverted index


.


## Run PromQL queries against Elasticsearch


PromQL (GA) now covers about 92% of the queries used in the top 100 Grafana dashboards, up from 43.4% in Elasticsearch 9.4. The additions include vector matching and` label_join` ,` label_replace` , as well as functions such as` topk` . You can point existing dashboards at Elasticsearch without rewriting queries, and an automated A/B test against native Prometheus checks that results match. Learn[how we built PromQL into Elasticsearch](https://www.elastic.co/search-labs/blog/promql-elasticsearch-compute-engine) .


## Multiuser chat in Kibana


Kibana chats now support multiple users in the same conversation (in technical preview). Access can be set three ways: public to all users, restricted to specific users in an organization, or private. Your Elasticsearch agents can now work with your whole team in the same conversation. Any participant in the chat can prompt the agent, and all the users in the conversation see the response. Read more in the[deep dive blog](https://www.elastic.co/search-labs/blog/agent-builder-conversation-sharing) .


## Generate custom Kibana dashboard panels by prompting


You can now prompt Kibana chat to generate custom visualizations, built from HTML, CSS, and ES|QL queries (in technical preview). These behave like the native panels that are already part of Kibana. When a custom panel has a query, the date picker,[Kibana Query Language (KQL)](https://www.elastic.co/docs/explore-analyze/query-filter/languages/kql) bar, standard controls, and ES|QL variables all work as you’d expect. That lets you go from idea to dashboard in minutes, without a template or any frontend development. Dashboard banners with animated images and custom logos, flowcharts of data flows, scorecards with badges, and funnels are all possibilities. To learn more, check out the[feature blog](http://elastic.co/search-labs/blog/kibana-custom-panels-ai-dashboard-visuals) .


## Turn PDFs into Markdown with the document_extraction task type


1. Extract. From a PDF, get clean Markdown:


```text
POST _inference/document_extraction/<eis-endpoint-id>
{
"input": "https://example.com/elasticsearchnotes.pdf"
}


// Response: clean Markdown for the whole document 1 "
// # Elasticsearchnotes\n\n## Highlights\n...
```


2. Index and embed:


```text
PUT docs
{
"mappings": {
"properties": {
"content": {"type": "semantic_text" }
}
}
}


POST docs/_doc
{
"title": "Elasticsearchnotes",
"Content": "# Elasticsearchnotes\n\n## Highlights\n..."
}
```


3. Retrieve:


```text
GET docs/_search
{
"Query": {
"semantic": {
"field": "content",
"Query": “what’s new for OCR in 9.6?"
}
}
}
```


` document_extraction` is a new inference task type (in technical preview) for Elastic Inference Service (EIS) that brings the document processing capabilities of Jina Reader to Elasticsearch. When you send one request with a PDF URL, you get clean Markdown back. It also handles scans of other document types via a URL or Base64. This new task type builds upon the recently released` jina-ocr-v1` model by managing pre- and post-processing needed to feed PDFs and other document types into the model, so you make a single request and skip building a processing pipeline. You can optionally feed the output to a` semantic_text` field to handle embedding


the content for search and agent workflows. To learn more, check out the detailed blog about[document_extraction](https://www.elastic.co/search-labs/blog/document-extraction-pdf-markdown-elasticsearch) and the blog about[jina-ocr-v1](https://www.elastic.co/search-labs/blog/ocr-model-jina-ocr-v1-document-parsing) . This feature will be available as part of the 9.6 release in early December.


### Non-streaming chat completion for regulated and air-gapped deployments


Non-streaming chat completion (GA) returns a complete model response in a single synchronous reply instead of in a stream of chunks. This matters for organizations that route inference traffic through a proxy which doesn’t support HTTP streaming, such as the data loss prevention (DLP), content-inspection, and audit-logging proxies common in regulated environments. This also helps on-premises or air-gapped deployments running models locally where networking or middleware can’t support streaming connections. Elastic[Agent Builder](https://www.elastic.co/elasticsearch/agent-builder) and other chat-based Kibana features now work in these deployments. This feature will be available as part of the 9.6 release in early December.


### Cut cost and latency with opt-in prompt caching


Opt-in prompt caching (in technical preview) reduces cost and latency


for multi-turn[agentic workflows](https://www.elastic.co/search-labs/blog/ai-agentic-workflows-elastic-ai-agent-builder) , including Agent Builder and direct Inference API use with Anthropic models. Callers mark the portions of a request that they want cached, and session IDs improve the odds of a cache hit across turns. This works best with large, stable system prompts and tool definitions.This feature will be available as part of the 9.6 release in early December.


## Run workflows on Elastic Service Accounts, and track spend with budget alerts


Elastic Service Accounts (GA) let admins bind scheduled[Elastic Workflows](https://www.elastic.co/search-labs/blog/elastic-workflows-automation) to a role-scoped identity created in Kibana, so automation keeps running when its author changes teams. A role change or deletion applies to every workflow bound to the account. In 9.6, binding is limited to Workflows and requires the` manage_security` permission.


Administrators also get more control over spend and records of change:


-


**Budget alerts (GA)** support daily, monthly, quarterly, and yearly periods with custom start dates.


-


**Serverless log delivery (GA)** sends audit logs to a destination with its own retention policy.


-


**Elastic Cloud audit trail (GA)** gives administrators a searchable record of who changed deployments and organization settings, in GovCloud.


-


**Elastic Agent** supports FIPS 140-3 for regulated environments, and Managed Integrations are available in GovCloud.


## Get started with Elasticsearch 9.6


Ready to get started? *These and other 9.6 capabilities are now available in serverless, except where noted. 9.6 is expected to be available for ECH and Self-Managed deployments in early December.*
